name_reason: Follows fd2_<domain>_<descriptor> convention: domain=ani_decoder, descriptor=chunk_row_decode_rle. No Ghidra address residue. Name accurately reflects the role: dispatch-table chunk handler ('chunk') that RLE-decodes ('decode_rle') into the destination row buffer ('row'), as opposed to its palette-targeting sibling fd2_ani_decoder_chunk_palette_load_rle @ 0x36B0F. Consistent with the other chunk handlers in anidec.c.
purpose: ANI frame-decoder chunk handler: RLE-decode exactly target_width bytes from the stream into the destination row buffer.
logic_summary: dst = data_fd2_animation_ani_decoder_dst_buf; width = data_fd2_animation_ani_decoder_target_width; pos = 0. Loop while pos < width: read byte b from the stream cursor; if (b & 0xC0) == 0xC0 it is a run token (run_len = b & 0x3F): advance pos by run_len, read the fill byte, memset run_len copies of fill at dst, advance dst by run_len; otherwise b is a literal: write b to dst, pos++, advance dst. Binary emits the run via REP STOSW + trailing STOSB (run_len total bytes) which is equivalent to the memset; identical RLE format as the palette variant @ 0x36B0F, differing only in output target (row buffer vs 768-byte palette area).

returns.semantics: No return value. Side effects: writes exactly target_width bytes into the destination row buffer (data_fd2_animation_ani_decoder_dst_buf) and advances the shared stream cursor (g_ani_cursor, modelling ESI in the binary) by a variable number of consumed bytes.

reads_globals: g_ani_cursor (file-scope static stream cursor modelling ESI; advanced by the handler)
writes_globals: g_ani_cursor (file-scope static; advanced as the stream is consumed)
notes: Only referenced from the frame dispatch table slot @ 0x52782 (+0x18); no direct callers (invoked indirectly via fd2_ani_decoder_decode_frame_bytes @ 0x36C9E). Source comment block (anidec.c lines 188-193) is already concise and correct (RLE decode target_width bytes to row buffer; C0-FF run header; cross-refs palette RLE), so it was kept; the detailed Ghidra plate is consistent with the refined understanding and was left untouched. The binary's run output (REP STOSW + odd-trailing STOSB) is functionally equivalent to the source memset(dst, fill, run_len); no equivalence concern. Did not edit src/anim/anidec.c (comment kept); only the shard is committed.
